content: Long-term use of this medication requires regular laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney function assessments and complete blood counts, to monitor your health. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in the refrigerator and discard any unused portion after 14 days, as the drug loses its potency beyond this period. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of expired or unused medication. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Penicillin is an antibiotic used to treat and prevent a variety of bacterial infections. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Before taking penicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other penicillin-type antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, ampicillin), cephalosporins (e.g., cephalexin, cefuroxime), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as aspartame, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Shake the bottle well before each dose. This medication can be taken with or without food. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and mouth sores. Rarely, you may develop a harmless black, hairy tongue, which usually resolves after treatment. Maintain good oral hygiene by brushing your tongue with a soft toothbrush twice daily. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during or weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Penicillin may interfere with live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, reducing their effectiveness. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. In case of an overdose with severe symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication is prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor.
